text:
kai: FYI — seeing a spike of GPU attach failures in us-west2 started ~07:13 UTC. Correlating with local NVMe IOPS spikes on scratchpool nodes. ops-bot posted alert: `gpu-attach-failures` 50 in 5m. Looks like a backscatter effect from cleanup jobs.

ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-attach-failures (us-west2) count=50 window=5m severity=high link=https://grafana/redwood/alerts/3456 :rotating_light:

dana: graph quick check — scratchpool iops 2k -> 22k at 07:12, fio-like burst pattern, scrub throughput ramped around same time. janitor pods show sustained disk writes.

maria: SMARTs show temp rise on affected hosts (194 -> 205) and a small uptick in media errors (retries). Not full failures yet but enough to blow up attach latency.

ajay: probable cause = cleaner/scrub cadence overlapping with GPU attach waves. We saw similar 'write-backscatter' in tests when many small-file deletes + scrub triggered. Short-term mitigation: throttle janitor in us-west2 to reduce parallelism. Suggest config patch: 
```yaml
janitor:
  rate_limit_qps: 6
  max_concurrency: 2
  backoff_ms: 250
```
Apply to canary 5 nodes first. Also add a circuit-breaker on attach path to fallback to warm pool when local attach latency > 300ms.

kai: I patched canary group (5 nodes) with `rate_limit_qps=6` at 07:28. Attach failures dropped from 50->4 in the next 10m. GPU attach latency 700ms -> 180ms median. Janitor CPU spiked on patched pods (they slowed, so more CPU waiting).

dana: good signal. We should still avoid blanket throttle globally — need a regional dynamic policy that watches local iops and temp. Also schedule major scrubs off-peak. For now, schedule an emergency cadence shift for us-west2 to run scrubs at 03:00 UTC.

maria: logging snippet from host-gnode-42 at 07:12: 
```
[07:12:11] janitor: start sweep /scratch/tmp (concurrency=12)
[07:12:14] nvme: iops burst 22000, queue_depth=512
[07:12:45] gpu-attacher: attach timeout retry=1 host=gnode-42
```
This is the backscatter pattern — cleanup starts, I/O queue backs up, attach times out.

ajay: plan: 1) roll regional throttle (us-west2) for next 24h; 2) implement attach fallback to warm/dedicated pool (short term); 3) add probe that triggers when scratchpool_iops > 10k and attach_failures > 5 in 5m (calls ops runbook). I'll open ticket INFRA-16233 and assign owners.

kai: running the fallback patch now (canary) — routing attaches to warm-pool when local attach > 400ms. Observed warm-pool absorb with small cost bump but keeps apps alive.

dana: ops notes for follow-up: - postmortem and root-cause: why cleaner concurrency default was 12 in region; revisit heuristics that scale concurrency by free-space instead of observed iops. - telemetry: add `backscatter_index` metric = scrub_rw_bytes / attach_ops over window.

maria: agreed. Also add a temporary alert: `scratchpool_backscatter_warning` when backscatter_index > 0.8 and SMART temp > 200.

ajay: opened INFRA-16233, added owners: @kai (mitigation), @dana (telemetry + schedule), @maria (postmortem writeup). So far canary looks stable. We'll roll region-wide in staged fashion with 10% -> 50% -> 100% over next 2 hours.

ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED INFRA-16233 https://redwood/infra/tickets/16233 created by ajay assigned=[kai,dana,maria] priority=P1

kai: tl;dr — immediate mitigation worked (throttle + fallback), next steps: telemetry + change default janitor concurrency heuristics. Will follow up with postmortem after soak. :thumbsup:

maria: adding note — cost impact: warm-pool fallback estimated +4% monthly on affected tenants during event window, but prevents customer impact.

dana: heads-up to SRE-oncall: we'll run controlled soak tomorrow 02:00 UTC, invite platform-team to monitor.

ajay: assigned runbook tasks, closing slack loop. If anyone sees regressions ping #eng-oncall and cc @kai.

(emoji thread reactions: :white_check_mark: :wrench: )
